one_liner: OpenGL shader port of Chlumsky's MSDF glyph generator; first-party chart shows 60x-132x faster than single-threaded msdfgen on one laptop.
what_it_does: A C library that loads a TrueType font through FreeType, generates multi-channel signed distance field (MSDF) glyphs straight into a GPU atlas texture with an index texture buffer, and renders text from them with its own shaders. Calls: msdfgl_create_context (compiles the shaders for GLSL '330 core', '330' or '320 es'), msdfgl_load_font or msdfgl_load_font_mem, msdfgl_generate_glyphs or msdfgl_generate_glyph_list (or a missing-glyph callback for on-demand generation), and msdfgl_render or msdfgl_printf to draw. It does not replace msdfgen's Shape/Bitmap API, because the output stays on the GPU and never comes back as CPU bitmaps.
how_it_is_fast: msdfgen's per-pixel stage runs as a fragment shader, one fragment per atlas texel, with one two-triangle draw call per glyph. That stage covers true and pseudo distance to every edge, the overlapping-contour inner/outer combine, and the median. Outlines are serialized on the CPU into an R8UI metadata buffer and an R32F point buffer that the shader reads with texelFetch. The CPU only decomposes outlines with FreeType, computes contour winding and runs msdfgen-style corner-based edge coloring. The shader also does less work than the baseline: it computes in 32-bit float rather than msdfgen's double, and it has no error-correction pass.
when_to_use: An application already rendering with OpenGL 3.3 core or OpenGL ES 3.2 that wants MSDF text built at runtime, including on-demand glyphs through msdfgl_set_missing_glyph_callback, instead of shipping a prebaked atlas.
Large glyph scales or big glyph sets, where CPU msdfgen takes seconds (README: 7.74 s at scale 4 against 0.0645 s for msdfgl).
TrueType fonts with quadratic outlines for Latin-like scripts (the benchmark font is DejaVu Sans).
C code bases that want a small MIT library whose only external dependency is FreeType (glad is vendored).
when_not_to_use: OpenType/CFF fonts with cubic outlines are unsupported, and the failure is unsafe. From the code: msdfgl_serialize_glyph sets FreeType's cubic_to callback to NULL, and FT_Outline_Decompose calls it without a check, so generating a cubic glyph should crash. The size pass's error is ignored first, so serialization also writes into a zero-size buffer slot. Convert fonts to quadratic first (cu2qu is suggested in issue #8).
Real text layout: there is no shaping (no HarfBuzz), only optional FreeType kerning, so no ligatures, bidi or complex scripts. Multiline printf is only an open PR (#15).
Offline atlas baking, headless or CPU-only pipelines, WebGL, Metal or Vulkan-only renderers. A GL context is required, and the text renderer uses a geometry shader (issue #3, open).

Ornamental, symbol or CJK glyphs with long contours. From the code: corner indices go into a fixed int corners[30] stack array with no bounds check, and per-contour segment and contour counts are stored in a char. char is signed on x86, so counts over 127 skip CPU coloring, while the GPU reads the same bytes as unsigned 8-bit.

When output must match msdfgen quality. There is no error-correction pass. Teardrop contours with 1 or 2 segments print 'Non-supported shape' and are left uncoloured, and wrong-winding detection is a README TODO. The shader math is declared precision mediump float, which GLES drivers that honour it may run at reduced precision.

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (CMake, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS defaults to ON)
integration.dependencies: FreeType 2.9.1+ (CMake downloads 2.10.1 if none is found), glad (vendored), an OpenGL 3.3 core or OpenGL ES 3.2 context; glfw only for the example
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (c_std_11), CMake 3.11; README reports a 32-bit MSVC 2019 build on Windows
integration.platforms: Linux (Wayland EGL with GLES 3.2, or GL 3.3 core with glfw3), macOS Mojave (deprecated OpenGL), Windows 10; README says it was tested only on Intel GPUs
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Every call needs the caller's current GL context, and msdfgl_printf and msdfgl_geometry use a function-static wchar_t[255] buffer for MSDFGL_WCHAR strings, so they are not reentrant.

gotchas: Shader compilation takes close to a second (README) and happens in msdfgl_create_context. Create the context once; the benchmark excludes this time.

msdfgl_generate_* only queues GL commands; there is no glFinish. A CPU timer around the call measures submission rather than GPU completion. The README says it averaged 100 runs and subtracted context creation and destruction time, but the benchmark code is not published.

Likely edge-colouring bug (found by reading msdfgl_serializer.c, not tested): when detecting corners, the start-of-contour tangent takes its point count from the second-to-last segment (meta_index + 2 * (nsegments - 2) + 1) while the pointer sits on the last segment. When those two segments differ in type (line and quad), the tangent is wrong, and it can read the next contour's first point. That can misplace a colour switch and produce corner artifacts. It affects output quality, not the timings.
The atlas texture is GL_RGBA32F (16 bytes per texel), and its height doubles as glyphs are added. Generation fails once the height passes GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: fontdue, font-rs and TiTanF rasterize coverage bitmaps on the CPU at a fixed pixel size, and Pathfinder 3 is a general Rust GPU vector rasterizer. Pick msdfgl for a C program on OpenGL 3.3 or ES 3.2 that wants one runtime-built atlas that stays sharp at any text size.
verified_claims_summary: The only evidence is the first-party README chart; there is no benchmark code, no compiler or flags, and no msdfgen version. Setup: ASCII 0-127 of DejaVu Sans, mean of 100 runs, Core i7 '8550m' with Intel UHD Graphics 620 on Debian. msdfgl takes 0.0081 s to 0.2345 s across scales 1 to 8, against 0.4890 s to 31 s for msdfgen (60x to 132x) and 0.1334 s to 8 s for OpenMP msdfgen (16x to 34x); both msdfgen values at scale 8 are extrapolated. The comparison is not like-for-like in three ways. msdfgl's time includes having the result in a texture while msdfgen's excludes the upload. msdfgl skips the roughly one-second shader compile. In msdfgen v1.6 (April 2019), generateMSDF also runs msdfErrorCorrection by default, a step msdfgl lacks; whether the benchmark called generateMSDF is not stated.
status_note: Stale: the last commit is 2024-10-13 (a warning fix), the core code dates from 2019-2020, and 5 issues are open. It is MIT-licensed and small (about 1,550 lines of C plus shaders), so it can be vendored, but it needs fixes before it is safe on untrusted or CFF fonts.
